newsitem.title: FRANCE: French court puts off decision on Papon travel ban.
newsitem.headline: French court puts off decision on Papon travel ban.

text.p: A French court on Tuesday postponed a decision on whether to impose a travel ban on former cabinet minister Maurice Papon who is due to face trial for World War Two crimes against humanity on October 6.
The court, expected to announce its decision on Tuesday, said it would do so on Thursday.

The ban, which would require Papon to hand over his passport and keep French authorities informed of his movements, had been requested by the state prosecutor and by Nazi-hunter Arno Klarsfeld, a lawyer representing relatives of victims.

Papon, 86, is accused of ordering the deportation of 1,560 Jews, 223 of them children, to Nazi death camps when he was secretary-general of the Bordeaux region in 1942-1944 under the pro-Nazi Vichy regime.
He went on to an illustrious post-war career, serving as Paris police chief in 1958-1967 and budget minister in the 1970s, until his wartime activities became known in 1981.
